obtained.how: Wisconsin DNR's own copy of the species leaflet (dnr.wisconsin.gov)

bibliography.checked_against: the leaflet's first page (text and page image)
bibliography.note: By Paul Holtan; Wisconsin Department of Natural Resources, Bureau of Fisheries Management; PUB-FH-714 98Rev., October 1998; 6 pp. Add the publication number and URL; it can now be cited directly instead of 'via Jordan et al. 2009'. It is a popular angler leaflet with no data, sample sizes or citations (only an 'Additional reading' list).

claims.claim: fecundity 1,500–7,000 eggs (Holtan 1998, via Jordan et al. 2009)
claims.source_value: a female may produce between 1,500 and 7,000 eggs, depending on size and age
claims.quote: a female may produce between 1,500 and 7,000 eggs
claims.conditions: Wisconsin; general statement without data; reads as eggs released per female (Jordan et al. relay it as eggs released), not ovarian counts
claims.note: The Ontario LHD range beside it (2,451–10,633) may be ovarian fecundity; the two are not the same quantity. Holtan also gives 1,500 to almost 15,000 fry per nest, average about 8,000.

claims.source_value: nests built in colonies of a few to as many as 10–15 nests
claims.quote: The nests are built in colonies that may range from just a few

claims.claim: nests < 1 m deep on sand or gravel
claims.source_value: sand or gravel bottoms, in water 'anywhere from 6 inches to several feet deep' (0.15 m to more than 1 m)
claims.quote: anywhere from 6 inches to several feet deep, on sand or gravel bottoms
claims.conditions: general statement; nest building starts at 55–63 °F (12.8–17.2 °C)
claims.note: Sand or gravel is Holtan's; '< 1 m' is not — it is McPhail 2007 as relayed by Jordan et al. 2009 (Jordan's p. 5). Holtan's nest-building temperature, 12.8–17.2 °C, is lower than the row's 17–26 °C (Ontario LHD).

claims.claim: egg incubation 3–5 d (row sources include Holtan 1998 via Jordan et al. 2009)
claims.source_value: eggs hatch in two to three days, or longer depending on conditions
claims.quote: The eggs hatch in two to three days, or longer depending on conditions
claims.note: Jordan et al. 2009 write 'three to five days after fertilization' without attributing it to Holtan; Holtan says 2–3 d. Cite the 3–5 d to Jordan et al. (or its source) and give Holtan's 2–3 d separately, or drop Holtan from this cell.

claims.source_value: females leave after spawning; males stay and protect the eggs, sometimes the fry, returning strays in the mouth
claims.quote: males stay and are highly protective of the eggs
claims.conditions: general statement; no duration given (the row's 6.0 ± 0.4 d is Cooke et al. 2006)

notes: Other content: first-year length about 2 in (age 1: 2.1 in); most mature in the second or third year; maximum age 8–10 years; mature fish average 5–8 in and 8–12 oz; thrives at 75–89 °F; more tolerant of low O₂ than bluegill but less of warm water; adults rarely school (pairs or groups of 3–4), young form large inshore schools; homing after displacement within a lake. The weight '8-12 ounces' for 5–8-in fish looks high for a pumpkinseed; treat the leaflet's numbers as popular, not measured.
